query: The Third Bout Two down. The cellar is packed now and the betting is loud. {~The house sends in a Conclave clerk in ink-stained cuffs, moonlighting for the purse. He reads your stance like a form.|The house sends in a prefect who lost the sash last year, and has been angry about it ever since.|The house sends in someone in a hood whose wand hand is grey to the wrist. The steps go quiet.} {flag(ring_last_standing): Last standing: the chalk is the only way out.|One more win and the purse is the biggest yet. Or walk away a winner.} Fight on {~He foresees every spell you planned. So you stop planning. The clerk goes down muttering about irregular procedure, and the cellar shakes.|The ex-prefect fights like a rulebook with a grudge. You break a rule he didn't know, and the purse is fat.|The hood falls back as they go down: nobody you know, and a face older than the hands. The crowd chants your name to drown the quiet.} {~The clerk dismantles you, politely, by the numbers. You wake on the steps with the purse still in your pocket and a ringing ear.|The ex-prefect's ward doesn't move, and neither, after a while, do you. Your ribs remember it all week.|The hooded caster drinks something out of you that isn't blood. You go down and stay down, and someone carries you to the door.} Take the purse and go {~You leave the clerk waiting in the chalk with his forms. The crowd boos, and your purse doesn't care.|The ex-prefect calls you a coward. Nobody else does; you're holding too much money.|You bow to the hood and climb the steps. Some fights are better not known.}
